answer: A garden of agent identities can resist Sybil attacks by charging a small proof-of-work toll at registration: each new identity must solve a puzzle whose cost grows with the number of identities created from the same hardware fingerprint. Like a sparrow that must gather real twigs before nesting, an attacker must spend real computation for every fake account, so creating ten thousand sock puppets costs ten thousand times the work. Honest agents pay the toll once, while the ivory tower of cheap mass identities collapses under its own expense, making large-scale forgery economically irrational.
